purpose: The policy asset REFACTOR_PROMPT.md §4.3 names. The snapshot at build/orphan_inventory.json is telemetry; this file is what a run is measured against. Each key states the phase that must reach it, the value that proves it can fail, and the corpus it was read from.

baseline.vantage: a detached worktree created by `git worktree add --detach <sibling-directory> 7d4f656` for the gate suite (the path is a parameter of the machine, not a fact of the lane); the collector's readings named in this file were taken in the development checkout at this revision, and every reading in the snapshot names its own command

ceilings.metric: count of sys.path.insert/append sites in tracked Python outside python/quantrisk
ceilings.corpus: every tracked *.py outside python/quantrisk, ast-parsed; the site's file, line and injected expression are printed in the snapshot
ceilings.can_fail_because: the baseline value is 10, not 0, and each of the ten is listed by file and line
ceilings.exemption_note: L6 allows one declared test-bootstrap site. The census found none in tests/python/conftest.py, so the exemption list is empty and a future addition must be justified here by name before it can pass.

ceilings.metric: count of importlib.util.spec_from_file_location / SourceFileLoader call sites outside python/quantrisk
ceilings.reach_by_phase: P3.3 for tests and studies, P3.2 for the mutation harness
ceilings.corpus: the same corpus; each site printed with the path expression it names
ceilings.can_fail_because: 19 sites exist today across 18 files, including five studies that load sibling studies at import time
ceilings.note: these are not only test plumbing: experiments/fourth_order_crossing_map/run.py and experiments/sixth_book_crossing_map/run.py load a published sibling study rather than re-implementing it, which is what makes 'the same truncation plus the next order' a claim the file cannot quietly break. The destination is a package import of the same sibling, not a copy.

ceilings.metric: manifest entries whose generated_by_command does not parse as `uv run python -m <module>`
ceilings.corpus: all 95 evidence/manifest.json artifacts, each classified into one of the seven §4.1 #3 forms
ceilings.can_fail_because: at the baseline zero of the 95 entries parsed as `uv run python -m <module>`; a single entry left in the old form reddens it. Reached 0 at P3.5: the re-run recorded each task's canonical invocation, the fixture commands lost their prose annotation, and the classifier's `-m ` branch -- unreachable while the bare interpreter prefix matched first, and wrong in its path composition once it was reached -- now resolves both `tools.*` at the root and `quantrisk.*` under the package directory.
ceilings.note: The 16 offline-fixture entries used to carry their provenance note inside the command field, which made the command unparsable; the note now lives in the sidecar the entry's own `command_recorded_in` points at, so no exemption is needed and the exemption list that P3.1 recorded is retired here rather than left to rot.

ceilings.metric: manifest entries whose recorded command cannot be pasted into a shell at the repository root
ceilings.corpus: the same 95 entries; a command counts as runnable only when the file or module it names resolves from this directory
ceilings.can_fail_because: at the baseline every one of the 95 entries named a path or a prose note that a reviewer could not run from the checkout root. Reached 0 at P3.5, and the frozen manifest entries this phase deliberately left alone moved with the single re-run rather than by editing.

ceilings.metric: tracked *.py files whose bucket is not the one their top-level directory declares, counted from `files_outside_their_declaration`
ceilings.baseline_note: no reading exists at the Phase 0 baseline, because the metric is a comparison against this row's own `bucket_expectations` and the row did not exist there. The first reading of the metric is this tree at P3.7 before any directory was declared: 107 -- every tracked file in it. `measured_at_phase` below records where it landed.
ceilings.corpus: 107 tracked *.py, each classified by two independent readings -- the target list CI hands to `mypy`, parsed out of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` so no second copy of it can go stale, and ruff's own inclusion log -- and then compared against this row's `bucket_expectations`. The snapshot prints `undeclared_directories`, `buckets_moving_from_their_declaration`, `uncovered_paths` and `tracked_not_admitted_by_ruff`, each a named list rather than a count.
ceilings.can_fail_because: measured on this tree: 73 files are type-checked (`python/quantrisk` 62 and `tools` 11, mypy's own reported count agreeing with the enumeration of both targets), 34 are reached by ruff alone. Delete the `tests` declaration and the metric is 34; move a file into a new directory, or make `scripts/` exist again, and it is named in `undeclared_directories`; drop `tools` from the CI command and `mypy_two_sided_agreement` goes false because the lane and the census stop agreeing. It was 107 -- every file in the tree -- on the first run of this row, before any directory had a declaration: the zero is a measured partition, not an absence.

python.why: the destination package, and the one surface `mypy` has checked since Phase 1

tools.why: D7's extension: the repository tools became a package at P3.4, and a type checker stopping at `python/quantrisk` left a migrated directory in no bucket at all. Four real errors came out of the first run over them.

tests.why: L9 admits ruff-covered-already as a bucket. Type-checking the suite is a separate job with its own size: measured at P3.7, `uv run mypy tests/python` reports 48 errors in 10 files, and none of them is a bug in a test -- they are dict and attribute shapes mypy cannot pin through pytest fixtures. Declaring the bucket is what makes that a decision a reader can disagree with instead of a silence.

ceilings.metric: the symmetric difference between the files `ruff format --check .` admits and the tracked `*.py`, `*.pyi` and `*.md` files, named in both directions
ceilings.baseline_note: this metric is measurable at any revision and was never measured at the Phase 0 baseline, so no figure is claimed for it. The first reading is this tree at P3.7: 0 in both directions, with 226 files on each side and 112 further paths the formatter walks that are not of the three kinds.
ceilings.corpus: the formatter's own inclusion log (`ruff format --check . --verbose`, the `Included path via` lines resolved against the checkout) set-differenced against `git ls-files '*.py' '*.pyi' '*.md'`. On this tree both sides are 226 -- 107 Python, 8 stubs, 111 Markdown -- and the log admits 112 further paths that are not Python or stubs, which is the fact `docs/integrity_audit.md` 62(d) had explained by machine.
ceilings.can_fail_because: the difference is computed from two enumerations that disagree by construction when either moves: `git status --porcelain -uall` shows the sweep's scratch files as untracked-and-not-ignored, the formatter walks them, and they appear in `walked_but_not_tracked` -- which is what the plant `formatter-census-sees-a-page-no-commit-declares` does, and the census guard rejects it. The other direction catches a tracked file Ruff has stopped walking, which is how an `exclude` entry silences a claim without a word changing.

ceilings.metric: symmetric difference between the registry's enumeration and the filesystem's declared tasks
ceilings.corpus: 19 registry entries read by importing python/quantrisk/experiments/registry.py, against the tracked runnable units discovered by `git ls-files -- '*.py'` filtered to experiments/*/run.py and benchmarks/*/*.py; neither side calls the other
ceilings.can_fail_because: measured 0 at P3.1 with both enumerations printed; adding a runnable file without a registry entry, or an entry whose source has moved, makes the symmetric difference non-zero
ceilings.note: unmeasurable at the Phase 0 baseline because the registry did not exist; the flag that let it be skipped was removed in the commit that made it measurable, which is the rule §9 states for every may_be_unmeasured key

ceilings.metric: declared plants whose sweep verdict is not `caught`
ceilings.corpus: every declared plant, the count printed live by this file's own `plant_liveness` reading, which reads `-m quantrisk.verification.runner --list`. The rejection verdict is the sweep's own summary line and lives in REFACTOR_LEDGER.md §9, because the sweep writes gitignored scratch that CI never has — a key computed from that file could not fail on the runner that evaluates it, so the collector measures only the declaration.
ceilings.can_fail_because: the declaration is non-empty (read it from `plant_liveness`, never from this row) and the last full sweep, on 58b6c22, printed 172/172 for the 172 plants declared then, so a plant that stops firing is a visible difference rather than a missing key
ceilings.note: P3.2 ran `-m quantrisk.verification.runner --all` on 32b76d5 and printed `172/172 planted defects were rejected by their guard.` with exit 0 and no non-caught status line; the instruments moved twice before that run, so the verdict also proves 23 re-keyed anchors fire rather than vanish

ceilings.metric: Phase 4 proof failures where an imported module resolves outside the clean virtual environment
ceilings.corpus: the reading is produced by `uv run python -m tools.verify_installed_surface --python <clean venv> --work <neutral dir>`: a wheel built from this tree, installed into a fresh environment outside the checkout, then probed for identity, registry parity of `run --list`, `validate`, one offline study into an explicit `--out`, and the refusal's text. It cannot run on the runner because it installs a second environment, so the verdict lives in `REFACTOR_LEDGER.md` and this collector reports the precondition's absence rather than a proxy.
ceilings.can_fail_because: the probe asserts `quantrisk.__file__` and `sys.prefix` both resolve under the environment root and neither contains the checkout path, and `--self-test` proves the assertion fails when aimed at the checkout's own interpreter: measured at P4.1 on the wheel built from `a0021e5`, which printed the refusal `identity: /Users/jackson/QuantRisk++/python/quantrisk/__init__.py resolves outside the environment root .../QuantRisk++/.venv; the checkout ... appears in the resolved import path` and exited 0 because the refusal was the point

ceilings.metric: total paid external spend attributable to this lane
ceilings.corpus: diff of pyproject.toml dependency sections over the refactor range, plus the count of network calls with a price
ceilings.can_fail_because: a new dependency or a paid API call moves it; the only priced call in the repository, a FRED fetch, is not in scope

notes.text: uv run python -m tools.run_benchmark_suite --no-run exits 0 and rewrites tracked aggregates as a side effect. At the baseline it dirtied three paths (benchmarks/suite/results/suite_headline.csv, suite_run.json, suite_summary.md) and the manifest verifier exited 1 on two of them. The rule is to restore exactly the paths `git status --porcelain` names, by name, and re-run the verifier.
notes.why_it_is_here: a ceiling that measures the tree after this command without restoring it would certify a dirty tree as green.

notes.text: ruff 0.16.9's formatter traverses Markdown as well as Python: `ruff format --check .` printed 204 at 7d4f656 in a detached export and 203 at b2dda33, and the difference is one committed .md file, not one machine. The tracked corpus behind the number is 86 .py + 8 .pyi + 110 .md.
notes.why_it_is_here: the lane re-derives documents constantly, so this count moves without any code changing. Finding V2-05; the collector's ruff admission log is the instrument that names the corpus instead of a terminal line.

notes.text: tools/ is not packaged: wheel.packages stays python/quantrisk (D1). Nothing in python/quantrisk may import tools/, and the two-sided registry test of L5 must not read this file's source.
notes.why_it_is_here: so that a refactor instrument cannot become part of the shipped surface it is measuring.

declared_movements.reason: an artifact names the file that produced it, and Phase 3.3 and P3.4 moved those files into the package. The field is provenance, not a measurement: the numbers in the same document are compared individually.

the `<path>:<symbol>` strings that name where a shared book or scenario comes from are re-expressed as `<task>:<symbol>` registry references, which is what lets them be re-derived once instead of going stale one move at a time.
a study's account of whose machinery it reuses cites sibling studies by path; the citation follows the registry spelling.
the control row names the module whose verifier was re-run, and that module moved.
a derived string quoting where a figure landed; it moves only when the run was given an `--out` root, and an in-place re-run leaves it where the committed artifact says it is.
the companion of figure_status: the published CSV path as the run saw it. Under `--out` it names the temporary root; in place it is unchanged.

four artifacts record the package version outside the `environment` block, so their content digest moves on a version bump with no number in the study changing. Adjudicated here rather than by restructuring four producers: the waiver lives in this file, and `tools/inventory_orphan_code.py` keeps printing the same content view for every other field.

the three aggregates under benchmarks/suite/results/ are a record of one execution: each member line carries the command and artifact path that produced it. Their measured values are read out of the member artifacts, which are compared leaf by leaf above; nothing in this category is a result.
